title: Dedicated staged rollouts — load test plan (reserved pools)
content:
Goal / why this doc exists
We need a repeatable load test suite that exercises Dedicated staged rollouts end-to-end on a reserved pool (routing weights + gate evaluator + approvals + autoscaling guardrails) to answer:
1) At what traffic levels do partial stages saturate a pool / cause queuing?
2) Do gates pause/hold fast enough to prevent SLA-impacting degradation?
3) Does routing allocation remain deterministic and tenant-isolated under stress?
4) Are metrics + evaluator robust to missing/late signals?

This is NOT a generic performance test of inference. It’s a “rollout mechanics under load” test.

Scope
- Dedicated pools only (reserved GPU pools). No hosted/shared.
- Control plane primitives (RolloutPlan/Stage/Gate), routing enforcement of weights, evaluator behavior, autoscaling headroom policies.
- Focus on failure modes: queue depth, evaluator lag, missing metrics, race conditions with approvals.

Assumptions
- We have a test Dedicated pool in staging that resembles prod pool shape (same GPU type if possible; if not, scale targets accordingly).
- Workload is token streaming chat or text gen (choose one primary path; embeddings optional).
- We can generate controllable traffic with a fixed prompt set and fixed output token targets to reduce variance.

Definitions (for this plan)
- “Pool saturation”: queue depth rising monotonically for > N minutes OR GPU utilization pegged + latency tail blows up.
- “Stage weight”: percent of pool traffic routed to new version; remainder to baseline.
- “Gate evaluation window”: the aggregation window used by evaluator (ex: 5m rolling) and the required consecutive pass periods.
- “Hold”: automatic pause (stop auto-advance) when a gate fails or metrics are missing/late.

Test environments / pre-reqs
Environment
- Staging Dedicated control plane
- 1 dedicated pool (pool_id: DED-STG-ROLL-01) with reserved capacity
- 2 model versions (baseline + candidate). Candidate should be “safe but slightly worse” for at least one scenario (e.g., +10–20% latency) OR we inject delay.

Feature flags / config
- staged_rollouts_dedicated_enabled = true
- per-tenant allowlist enabled for test tenant
- autoscaling headroom guardrails enabled (min headroom policy toggles per scenario)

Rollout plan used (default)
- Stage 0: internal shadow (0% external) — optional (depends on plumbing)
- Stage 1: 5% for 20m
- Stage 2: 25% for 30m
- Stage 3: 100%
- Manual approval required to advance Stage 2->3 (simulate enterprise governance)

Default gates (recommended for load tests)
- Latency gate: p95 end-to-end latency <= baseline_p95 * 1.15 (or absolute threshold per pool)
- Error gate: 5xx rate <= 0.5% AND timeout rate <= 0.3%
- Queue depth gate: p95 queue_depth <= X (pool-specific) OR queue_depth slope <= 0 (no sustained growth)
- Utilization gate: GPU utilization <= 92% (sustained) (guardrail; exact number TBD)
- Metrics freshness gate: evaluator must have all required metrics within 2x scrape interval; missing => HOLD (fail-safe)

NOTE: use whatever is in dedicated-rollouts-gating-slos as the source of truth; above is for planning.

Instrumentation checklist (must-have)
Routing / rollout state
- [ ] Current rollout plan version, stage id, stage start timestamp
- [ ] Effective stage weights at router (what router thinks, not just control plane desired)
- [ ] Deterministic allocation sanity: same request key consistently maps to same backend version across restarts
- [ ] Fallback counters: how often we fall back from candidate->baseline due to capacity / errors

Gate evaluator
- [ ] Evaluator tick duration (p50/p95)
- [ ] Evaluator lag: “now - latest metric timestamp consumed”
- [ ] Gate evaluation outcome per gate (pass/fail/unknown) + reason codes
- [ ] Hold transitions: timestamp + gate that triggered
- [ ] Missing metric counters by metric name

Pool health / performance
- [ ] Request rate (RPS), token rate (tokens/s), avg prompt tokens, avg output tokens
- [ ] End-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99) by version (baseline vs candidate)
- [ ] 5xx rate, timeout rate, cancellations
- [ ] Queue depth distribution (p50/p95/p99) and queue time if available
- [ ] GPU utilization, memory utilization, KV cache pressure (if exposed), OOM / evictions
- [ ] Pod/container restarts, node-level throttling

Autoscaling / capacity guardrails
- [ ] Headroom estimate (available capacity vs load)
- [ ] Scale decisions + cooldowns (even if reserved pool has limited scaling, we still need “guardrail triggers”)
- [ ] Guardrail blocks: attempts to advance stage that were rejected due to headroom policy

Audit / approvals
- [ ] Approval event emitted with correct actor + timestamp + stage id
- [ ] Concurrent approvals idempotency: repeated approve calls do not double-advance

Traffic generator
- [ ] Reproducible config: seeds, prompt set IDs, target concurrency
- [ ] Client-side latency histograms and errors (to correlate with server metrics)

Test data to record every run
- Run ID
- Pool_id, tenant, region
- GPU type / pool shape
- Baseline model + candidate model identifiers (and runtime config)
- RolloutPlan JSON (as applied)
- Gate thresholds
- Traffic profile
- Start/end time
- Summary (pass/fail) + notes

Core scenarios
Scenario 1 — Baseline capacity characterization (no rollout)
Purpose: find safe operating envelope + the knee where queueing starts.
Steps
1) Route 100% traffic to baseline only.
2) Sweep load: increase concurrency in steps (ex: +10% every 10m) until p95 latency grows > 2x OR queue depth p95 > threshold.
3) Record “knee point” and “saturation point”.
Outputs
- Baseline max sustainable RPS and tokens/s at acceptable tail latency.
- Queue depth vs RPS curve.
Pass criteria
- We can identify a stable operating point and a clear onset of queuing.

Scenario 2 — Staged rollout at low load (control case)
Purpose: validate stage transitions and observability without hitting capacity limits.
Traffic: 30–40% of baseline max sustainable load.
Steps
1) Create rollout plan, Stage 1 5%.
2) Let evaluator run; confirm gates pass; auto-advance to Stage 2 (25%).
3) Require manual approval for Stage 3; approve after 10m.
Outputs
- Stage state machine transitions with timestamps.
- Gate evaluation traces show consistent pass.
Pass criteria
- Auto-advance occurs only when gates pass for the full evaluation window.
- Manual approval advances exactly once and is auditable.

Scenario 3 — Staged rollout near saturation (“partial stage overload”)
Purpose: validate that partial rollout doesn’t accidentally exceed headroom and that guardrails prevent unsafe stage progression.
Traffic: 80–90% of baseline max sustainable load (from Scenario 1).
Hypothesis
- At 25% stage weight, the candidate portion may saturate if candidate is slower OR if routing causes uneven distribution.
Steps
1) Start at Stage 1 (5%) at high traffic.
2) Observe queue depth/latency by version.
3) Attempt to auto-advance to 25% and then 100%.
Expected
- Either: gates fail at Stage 2 due to queue depth/latency and rollout enters HOLD, OR guardrail blocks stage advance.
Pass criteria
- Rollout does not proceed to the next stage when there is sustained queuing or latency regression.
- HOLD happens within <= 2 evaluator windows (target; tune based on ADR + SRE signoff).
- No “thrash”: repeated advance/hold oscillation.

Scenario 4 — Induced regression (candidate slower)
Purpose: validate signal sensitivity; we need a known-bad candidate.
Method
- Option A: candidate model intentionally heavier (larger context / disabled optimization)
- Option B: inject artificial per-request delay at candidate backend
Traffic: 50–70% of baseline sustainable.
Steps
1) Start rollout at 5%, allow it to stabilize.
2) Increase to 25%.
3) Observe p95 latency gate failure and HOLD.
Pass criteria
- Latency gate fails reliably and HOLD triggers.
- Stage weight freezes (no further shift) while on HOLD.
- Operator can abort/rollback cleanly and traffic returns to baseline.

Scenario 5 — Missing metrics (fail-safe)
Purpose: verify “missing metrics => HOLD” and UI reason is clear.
Method
- Temporarily block one metric series (e.g., queue depth) from being emitted OR break label match to simulate cardinality change.
Steps
1) Start Stage 1.
2) Remove metric feed for one required gate metric.
Expected
- Evaluator marks gate status as UNKNOWN/MISSING (whatever the spec says) and triggers HOLD.
Pass criteria
- Rollout pauses, does not advance.
- Alert fires for missing metrics (per dashboards spec).
- Once metrics restored, operator can manually resume (or auto-resume if supported; clarify desired behavior).

Scenario 6 — Evaluator lag / overload
Purpose: prevent repeats of dogfood incident where evaluator lag delayed pause.
Method
- Increase evaluator load (many rollouts in parallel in staging) OR throttle evaluator resources.
- Also run high RPS on pool.
Steps
1) Start rollout and induce candidate regression (Scenario 4-style).
2) Ensure evaluator tick is slow / lagging.
Expected
- System forces rollouts into HOLD if evaluator degraded (per fail-safe behavior PR).
Pass criteria
- “Evaluator degraded => HOLD” engages before rollout can proceed to more risky stages.
- Lag metrics clearly show breach; alerting triggers.

Scenario 7 — Approval race / concurrent actions
Purpose: verify idempotency and stage advancement correctness under concurrent approvals and evaluator ticks.
Steps
1) Configure Stage 2->3 to require manual approval.
2) At the time the evaluator would be eligible to advance (gates pass), submit multiple approvals concurrently (from two operator accounts / scripts).
3) Simultaneously run “abort” and “approve” in tight window (this is intentionally adversarial).
Pass criteria
- Exactly one terminal outcome (advanced OR aborted) per defined precedence rules.
- Audit log is consistent; no double-advance; no stage stuck-in-between.

Scenario 8 — Router restart / config propagation during rollout
Purpose: ensure determinism + no surprise traffic shifts.
Steps
1) Start rollout at Stage 2 (25%) under moderate load.
2) Restart routing component(s) or roll them during the test.
3) Confirm allocation remains stable and stage weights are preserved.
Pass criteria
- No sudden spike in candidate traffic above configured weight.
- No cross-tenant mixing (sanity check via tenant labels).

Scenario 9 — Capacity-constrained fallback behavior
Purpose: validate safe fallback when pool constrained (candidate portion fails open/closed appropriately).
Steps
1) Constrain candidate capacity (e.g., fewer replicas) while stage weight expects more.
2) Run steady traffic.
Expected
- Router falls back to baseline per policy; gate should catch if this impacts latency/errors.
Pass criteria
- Fallback counter increases; baseline absorbs without overload.
- Rollout does not keep advancing if it’s not truly exercising candidate at intended weight (open question: should we gate on “actual traffic share to candidate”?)

Expected saturation points / what we should measure
We should capture these as numbers per pool shape; below is guidance for analysis.

Key curves to produce
1) RPS vs queue_depth_p95 (baseline only)
2) tokens/s vs GPU utilization (baseline only)
3) For rollout stages: (candidate_share) vs (candidate_latency_p95) vs (pool_queue_depth)

Rule-of-thumb expectations (update after first run)
- The onset of queuing typically happens when sustained GPU utilization is > ~90–95% depending on batching behavior.
- Partial stage saturation can happen even at lower pool-wide utilization if:
  - traffic hashing skews disproportionately to candidate replicas (bug / small sample)
  - candidate has less effective batching due to lower share
  - candidate is slower and starves queue

What “bad” looks like
- queue_depth_p95 grows steadily for > 5m
- timeout rate increases even if 5xx stays flat
- p99 latency spikes first, then p95 creeps

Pass/fail criteria (overall)
Hard pass criteria (must meet)
- Tenant isolation preserved: no evidence of cross-tenant routing or shared metrics leaking (spot check labels + audit tenant ids).
- Deterministic routing: stable assignment of request keys across retries/restarts at a given stage weight.
- Fail-safe behavior:
  - Missing metrics => HOLD (no auto-advance)
  - Evaluator degraded => HOLD (no auto-advance)
- Gate responsiveness: for induced regressions, HOLD occurs within acceptable detection time (target: <= 10m; calibrate to evaluation window + 1 tick).
- Abort/rollback: operator abort returns traffic to baseline and leaves system in consistent terminal state; audit events emitted.

Soft pass criteria (should meet; log follow-ups if not)
- Low false positives: at low/moderate load, gates should not HOLD due to noise.
- Alert quality: alerts fire with actionable reason (missing metrics, lag, gate failure type).
- No severe observability cardinality blow-ups from per-stage metrics.

Operational runbook tie-ins (who does what during the test)
- Driver (Infra): Keiko / Vanessa
- SRE observer: Sean (or delegate) monitors dashboards + validates alert behavior
- Telemetry: Logan / Thomas on standby if we see missing series / lag
- Routing: Mina / Elena if allocation looks off

During test, if HOLD triggers unexpectedly
1) Confirm metrics freshness / evaluator lag first.
2) Validate gate thresholds aren’t accidentally too strict for staging.
3) Inspect actual traffic split reaching candidate (effective share).
4) Decide: resume, adjust thresholds (only if justified), or abort.

Notes / open questions
- Do we need a gate on “actual candidate traffic share” to avoid advancing when candidate isn’t truly taking traffic? (e.g., candidate capacity constrained -> fallback hides it)
- Queue depth metric definition: is it per-router queue, per-backend queue, or global? Need consistency for gating.
- Staging GPU differences: if staging is smaller, should we scale thresholds linearly by tokens/s capacity or keep percent-based gates?
- For enterprise Dedicated, what’s the expected evaluation window default (5m vs 10m) and how does it trade off detection vs false positives?

Appendix A — Traffic generator config (placeholder)
- Prompt set: “dedicated-rollout-loadtest-v1” (10 prompts; mix short + long contexts)
- Target output tokens: 256 avg (cap at 512)
- Streaming enabled
- Concurrency ramp: +10 clients every 5 minutes
- Request key: stable user_id (to test deterministic hashing)

Appendix B — Quick run checklist
Pre-run
- [ ] Confirm pool_id + tenant
- [ ] Confirm dashboards links + alert routes
- [ ] Confirm feature flags and rollout plan JSON
- [ ] Confirm baseline and candidate versions deployed
- [ ] Warm up pool for 10m

Run
- [ ] Start traffic generator
- [ ] Execute scenario steps
- [ ] Record timestamps for stage changes, holds, approvals

Post-run
- [ ] Export graphs (latency, queue depth, evaluator lag)
- [ ] Summarize pass/fail
- [ ] File follow-ups against ENG-5130/ENG-5124/ENG-5123 as needed
